free_tier.stated: Free for reasonable public usage: a personal website or a small-to-medium business is fine, while sending millions of pageviews a day is not; no numeric cap is stated
free_tier.notes: Financed by donations through GitHub Sponsors. Several sites can share one account (Settings, sites). The hosted service and the open-source app share the same code; the hosted service is the offer recorded here.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-pageview or per-request size is stated on the pages read

retention.stated: unverified: no retention period of the hosted service is stated on the pages read; all data can be exported at any time

egress.terms: all data can be exported as CSV at any time, through the dashboard or the export endpoints of the API; the API allows 4 requests per second

interface_detail: REST API under /api/v0 on the account's own host (CODE.goatcounter.com), authenticated by an API key created in the account as a Bearer token (HTTP Basic also works); POST /api/v0/count sends pageviews from a backend in batches, POST /api/v0/export starts a CSV export, and GET endpoints list sites, paths and statistics. The browser side is one script tag, a no-JavaScript tracking pixel, backend middleware or log file import.
tooling: a single script tag, the tracking pixel, middleware or log file import for the data in, and any HTTP client with an API key for the data out. As a last resort the open-source app can be self-hosted: the user installs and runs it on a rented or free machine.
chaining: Pageview counting for a static site on any free host with one script tag and no cookies, with the numbers readable and exportable through the API.

limits.value: API: 4 requests per second, reported in the X-Rate-Limit response headers
free for reasonable public usage, with no number stated; millions of pageviews a day are outside it

limits_note: The backend count endpoint has higher rate limits than the browser endpoint and accepts several pageviews in one request.
binding_note: The only quota is the unstated reasonable-use ceiling; the 4-requests-a-second API limit binds only on programmatic reads.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for an account name, an optional site domain, an email address and a password of at least 8 characters, plus a human check that asks the visitor to type a shown number; no payment field appears on it.

reliability_note: no throttle, ban or data loss is stated on the pages read; the service is financed by donations
confidence_note: The free offer, the sign-up fields and the API limits are quoted from first-party pages. No account was opened and no numeric allowance or retention period is published, so both are unverified.

evidence.proved: the hosted service is free for reasonable public usage and millions of pageviews a day are outside that
evidence.quote: GoatCounter.com is currently offered for free for reasonable public usage. Running your personal website or small-to-medium business on it is fine, but sending millions of pageviews/day isn’t.

evidence.proved: the hosted service is financed by donations
evidence.quote: Donations are accepted via [Github Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/arp242/) to cover server costs.

evidence.proved: the app can be self-hosted from its GitHub repository
evidence.quote: You can [self-host GoatCounter](https://github.com/arp242/goatcounter) easily if you want to use it for more serious purposes.

evidence.proved: data can be exported and the account cancelled at any time
evidence.quote: Own your data; you can always export all data and cancel at any time.

evidence.proved: the browser side is a single script tag, with a no-JavaScript image tracker, middleware and log file alternatives
evidence.quote: The JavaScript integration is a good option for most, but you can also use a no-JavaScript image-based tracker, integrate in your backend middleware, or parse log files.

evidence.proved: the API is limited to 4 requests per second
evidence.quote: The rate limit is 4 requests per second; the current values are reported in the response headers:

evidence.proved: the API authenticates with a Bearer API key created in the account
evidence.quote: To use the API create a key in your account (`[Username in top menu] → API`); send the API key in the `Authorization` header as `Authorization: Bearer [token]`.

evidence.proved: HTTP Basic authentication with the API key as the password is also supported
evidence.quote: HTTP Basic auth is also supported; this is mostly useful for testing things from the browser. Leave the username empty and use the API key as the password.

evidence.proved: the count endpoint sends pageviews from a backend with higher rate limits and batching
evidence.quote: This is the same as `/count` that the JavaScript integration uses but has higher rate-limits, allows setting some additional fields, and allows batching multiple pageviews in one request.
